# Release safety annotations

## Upstream MIT fixtures (not the complete golden suite)

`upstream-mit/` contains immutable annotated **test data only**, derived from PTT, parse-torrent-name, go-ptn and scene-release-parser-php, via the fixed Guessit cross-parser data commit recorded in `manifest.json`. Each source retains its complete original MIT license and copyright. We do not vendor or execute any upstream parser. Files and license bytes have SHA-256 checks; the importer refuses existing destinations unless `--extend` explicitly validates their immutable hashes and only adds reviewed sources; it rejects redirects, oversized data and URL-like sensitive release names. `web/tests/import-release-corpus.mjs` is a development-only provenance import, not a test expectation generator.

The four sources have 763 entries and **683 unique inputs**; duplicate names never count twice. `TestMITCorpusAcceptedCoverageRespectsSpecifiedFields` compares source-provided season constraints and complete episode sets (not only safe subsets) for accepted coverage and prevents source-labelled TV from being accepted as a movie. Some upstream rows assert only a title, season, or episode: an omitted field is not a negative assertion. The independent oracle caught high-confidence first-episode-only results for `7x23-24` and `06x01-08`; v6 now parses those bounded ranges completely and holds leftover range/list fragments and ambiguous underscore coverage. `TestMITAcceptedYearMatchesIndependentEvidence` additionally checks explicitly annotated years without deriving expected values from PulseMedia. Those independent labels exposed titles containing calendar-like digits (Blade Runner 2049 / Wonder Woman 1984 / 2012 / 2047) being accepted with the wrong first year. v7 now holds distinct possible years rather than choosing the first/last, correctly recognizes underscore-separated unique years, and excludes identity numbers from calendar evidence. Explicit IDs cannot bypass review in automatic matching. Full exact title/quality/coverage/confidence/reason annotations and further independent inputs are still required for M3-02. Hash/provenance and partial safety assertions alone are **not 1000-case golden acceptance**; `formal_golden_acceptance` remains false.


` safety.jsonl ` contains 20 individually authored, fixed annotations using invented titles. They are not collected downloader URLs, MoviePilot resources, copyrighted media or a generated Cartesian product. The annotation fields are coverage/review/reason, checked independently of parser output; IDs and inputs must be unique. `independent_corpus_test.go` loads the committed bytes with strict JSON decoding and checks these contracts.

`ptt_original_year_test.go` separately preserves 13 original year/presence labels from `dreulavelle/PTT@88429bb90acef55673f421f45038878809b1e577/tests/test_year.py` (the same pinned MIT license/copyright already retained above). These are partial year-safety assertions, not full title/quality/confidence/reason goldens. The numeric television title `1923` exposed a spurious calendar attribute; parser v10 excludes a purely numeric title directly before an explicit season/episode token from year evidence. Multiple distinct possible dates still require review. A one-off, non-executing Python AST inspection of eight original test files found 460 unique names / 542 field labels, but only 54 names beyond the committed corpus (union 737), and no independent confidence/reason labels. Those review materials are not committed or accepted; the project does not acquire an unpinned Python runtime dependency. Missing labels must not be filled using PulseMedia parser output.


## Fully reviewed seed (361 entries, not acceptance)

`reviewed-full.json` contains 361 individually reviewed original MIT inputs from the hash-pinned sources explicitly admitted by the review loader; pending sources are not admitted merely by being recorded in the input pool. Each row retains its original input and source identifier, explicit review rationale, and the complete recognizer output contract: title/year/type, season, exact episode and unit sets, absolute number/anime flags, confidence/review/reason, and every quality attribute. No expected values are generated from PulseMedia outputs. `TestReviewedFullReleaseAnnotations` rechecks the source bytes/licenses through the shared provenance loader, requires the original input and independent title/year labels, rejects duplicate IDs/inputs or missing annotation fields, and checks exact quality values plus current observation versions. Unsupported audio, DVD and Xvid remain unknown, not silently converted to allowed properties.

The seed exposed BRRip source-family omission and release-group identities contaminated by `[ettv]`/`[rartv]` relay tags. Parser v14 preserves the original oracle and removes only known trailing distribution tags from new group observations. Negative group policy also checks decorated historical groups without rewriting saved evidence. BRRip does not assert encode fidelity or library ownership. The next seven original inputs independently caught release years left inside standard and alternate TV titles. Parser v15 separates only an unambiguous trailing release-year token from the series prefix; numeric work names and conflicting dates retain their safety rules. Identity suggestions use version v2 and still require the year to come from the work prefix, never just an episode subtitle. Nine additional pinned PTT inputs cover chained multi-episode sets, unbound absolute anime numbers, and DV/remux/cropped-quality facts. Parser v16 recognizes only bounded parenthesized resolution after an absolute number and excludes explicitly named audio channel multiplicities from coverage scanning without inventing audio facts. Unknown parentheses or conflicting coverage remain review-held. The full loader also checks original type, season and episode labels, including non-canonical absolute holds. The manifest explicitly reports **40 reviewed / 1000 required**, `formal_golden_acceptance=false`; this is a seed, not the complete M3-02 golden suite.

The four calendar-ambiguity rejection cases keep the original external title/year labels in their hash-checked source files. Optional `withheld_source_fields` declares only a refusal to emit those identity facts, not a corrected upstream value: it is permitted solely for zero-confidence, zero-year, zero-season, zero-episode/absolute/unit coverage, review-held `ambiguous_media_year` movie results. A retained display string is explicitly noncanonical. Accepted cases still require exact source title/year equality; missing, duplicate, unsupported and unnecessary exceptions are rejected. Fourteen guard tests cover attempted promotion. These cases exposed the known `[rarbg]` relay omission; v17 removes only this finite known tag from new observations, keeps unknown tags untrusted and retains legacy negative-group handling without rewriting stored evidence.

Ten additional independent pinned inputs cover explicit PROPER/REPACK revision markers, the word Half in a series title, French apostrophes/accents, Cyrillic work titles and ordinal prefixes, and titles with neither year nor quality. Revision markers do not assert edition or upgrade authority; DVD, codecs absent from the name, and unmeasured audio remain unknown. The dotted accented title is itself an original upstream input, not a locally generated variant. These brought the reviewed total to 35 at that stage; no independent specials input or new license source is claimed.

Five further original `go-ptn` inputs cover explicit H264/space-dash groups, unsupported HDRip/Xvid, absent resolution, spaced and dotted series acronyms, apostrophes and episode subtitles. They brought the fully reviewed total to 40 at that stage. Before comparing with the recognizer, the complete oracle now checks annotated resolution/source/codec against independent upstream labels; thirteen mutation-boundary tests reject promoted DVD/Xvid, contradictory attributes and unreviewed label vocabularies. Known unsupported facts may remain unknown; absent upstream labels cannot fabricate measurements.

Superseded v1 attributes decode as unknown without re-signing persisted JSON. Schema45 invalidates old ownership projections through evaluator v2; it does not manufacture new file facts or execution authority.
